items.label: Заметка

parts.html:
Ученику видна

Level: B1, adults

Dialect: British English

Time: 75 minutes

Goal: can describe childhood winter habits and traditions, share a specific memory and compare the past with the present

Grammar: used to / didn't use to / Did … use to?; Past Simple revision

Vocabulary: winter childhood activities and family traditions

Listening: three adults share their childhood winter memories

Speaking: talk about childhood winter habits, share a memorable event and compare past and present

items.label: Набор слов

parts.html:
• go sledging — to travel down a snowy hill on a sledge for fun
  • have snowball fights — to play by throwing balls of snow at each other
  • build snow forts — to make small walls or shelters using snow
  • wrap up warm — to put on warm clothes before going outside
  • spend hours outdoors — to spend a long time outside
  • warm up — to become warmer after feeling cold
  • stay indoors — to remain inside a building
  • family tradition — something a family does regularly, often on special occasions

parts.title: Teacher instructions
parts.html:
Ученику скрыта

Accept memories unrelated to snow or Christmas. Students may also invent a memory if they prefer.

One-to-one lessons:
Ask the student to select three objects and explain the memories they associate with them. Use the follow-up questions to explore the past and present.

Group lessons:
Students choose three objects individually, then share their memories in pairs. Invite a few students to compare their experiences.

Support for less confident students:
Provide the prompts This reminds me of… and When I was a child, I often…

Fast finishers extension:
Ask students to suggest one additional object they would put in the box and explain why.

Script
Speaker 1 — Oliver, 32
You know those winter days when you're meant to be home by lunchtime, but nobody checks the time? That was basically my childhood.
My cousins and I used to go sledging on the hill behind my aunt's house every Saturday. We'd wrap up warm and spend hours outdoors, even when our fingers were freezing.
One afternoon, my cousin decided we should build a snow fort at the bottom of the hill. It took ages.
Then Dad asked to have a go on the sledge. He came down much faster than he expected and went straight through our fort.
He was fine. The fort wasn't.
We laughed about that for years.
Speaker 2 — Priya, 36
My grandmother wasn't really a winter person. She hated icy pavements, so we didn't spend much time outside together. But she absolutely loved baking.

Every December, I used to spend an afternoon at her house making ginger biscuits. It was our family tradition. She kept the recipe on a little handwritten card, although she never followed it exactly.

items.label: Used to — Past habits and states
src: (template - picture
Used to — Past habits and states
We use used to to talk about regular actions and states in the past that are usually no longer true.
Affirmative
Subject + used to + base verb
We used to spend hours outdoors.
Negative
Subject + didn't use to + base verb
I didn't use to like cold weather.
Question
Did + subject + use to + base verb?
Did you use to go sledging?
Used to vs Past Simple

parts.title: Used to — Past habits and states
parts.html:
We use used to to talk about regular actions and states in the past that are usually no longer true.

| Form | Structure | Example |

| --- | --- | --- |

| Affirmative | Subject + used to + base verb | We used to spend hours outdoors. |

| Negative | Subject + didn't use to + base verb | I didn't use to like cold weather. |

| Question | Did + subject + use to + base verb? | Did you use to go sledging? |

Used to vs Past Simple

We used to build snow forts every winter. — a regular past habit

One winter, we built a huge snow fort. — a particular past event

Past Simple can also describe past habits. However, ‘used to’ emphasises that an action or state was common in the past and is usually different now.

We use Past Simple, not ‘used to’, for one particular event.

Language note

Used to can describe past states as well as repeated actions: I used to hate winter.

Past Simple can also describe past habits, but ‘used to’ makes the contrast with the present more noticeable.

Ex 1.3 Read Maureen's memories of an unusually cold winter in Britain. What is the main idea of her story?
What is the main focus of Maureen's story?
A. How one family managed without heating during a very cold winter
B. How people continued their everyday lives despite difficult weather
C. How schools and public transport prepared for a long period of snow
The Winter I'll Never Forget
When I was twelve, I lived in Berkeley, a small town in England. At Christmas in 1962, someone gave me a diary. Luckily, I wrote about the weather in it, so I still remember that unusual winter.

Heavy snow arrived just after Christmas and stayed for weeks. On New Year's Day, I bought a new pair of wellington boots because the snow was so deep. My young niece Susan was visiting, but she couldn't go home: the buses had stopped running. A few days later, the buses started again, and I travelled with her to Sharpness. But they stopped once more, so I had to stay there overnight.

School wasn't easy either. Our school bus was often late, and the classrooms were freezing. One day, after getting off the bus, I slipped on an icy road and made big holes in my new tights. We couldn't play games on the sports field because it was covered in snow, so we had lessons about sport instead.

Home wasn't particularly warm. We didn't have central heating, and even our bedrooms were cold. We used to put on extra layers of clothes and use hot-water bottles to keep warm. The coal fire helped, too.
Still, we didn't spend the whole winter at home. I went to the cinema with my friend Greta and even travelled to Bristol to see a show.

By February, I had stopped writing about the weather in my diary. Perhaps the snow had become so normal that there was nothing new to say. It finally started to get warmer in early March. I have never forgotten that winter.

Ex 1.5 A local museum is creating an online collection of childhood winter memories. Write a short story (100–130 words) for the exhibition
Include:
the activities or traditions you used to enjoy as a child
one particular winter day you remember
how your winters are different now
Use ‘used to’, Past Simple and some expressions from the lesson. You may invent a story if you prefer
Sample answer
The Winter We Built a Snow Fort
When I was a child, I used to spend hours outdoors with my neighbours. We loved having snowball fights and going sledging on a small hill near our houses.

One winter, we decided to build a huge snow fort. We worked on it all afternoon. Just as we finished, my little brother ran towards us and accidentally knocked down one of the walls. We were quite upset at first, but then we all started laughing. After that, we went inside to warm up and drink hot chocolate.
These days, I don't spend much time playing in the snow, but I still enjoy winter walks. That afternoon reminds me of how much fun we had without phones or computers.
